shared_elements: tall rectangular stone pillar/monolith standing in an excavated trench
quadruped animal carved in raised high relief clinging to the vertical face, head downward
flat low-relief / incised animal figures on the shaft below the high-relief animal
bird-like creature in profile (B) and animal profiles generally
dry-stone rubble walling and excavation debris surrounding the stone
pale beige limestone-like surface with weathered, pitted texture
justification: Both show a tall pale pillar rising from rubble walling with a quadruped in bold raised relief set high on the shaft above flatter, shallowly incised figures, and the combination of two relief depths on one vertical face is a fairly specific correspondence. The biggest difference is density and content: B is crowded with a horizontal register of animals, a zigzag band and multiple birds and beasts, while A is nearly bare apart from the single animal and the low-relief arm and hand, which has no counterpart in B.
